title: Spot the scam: inbox basics
intro: Your phone buzzes with four messages. Decide which are scams, spot the red flags and choose what to do. Some messages are genuine.
objective: Recognise common scam signals and learn that genuine messages exist too.

messages.body: CONGRATULATIONS!! Your number won ₹25,00,000 in the National Lucky Draw. Pay ₹5,000 processing fee today to claim. Reply YES now!
messages.explanation: You cannot win a lottery you never entered, and real prizes never charge a fee to release money.

messages.body: 482913 is your OTP to log in to Deccan Bank app. Do NOT share this OTP with anyone, including bank staff. -Deccan Bank
messages.explanation: This is an automatic OTP you requested. It warns you not to share it and asks for nothing. Use it yourself only in the official app.

messages.body: Dear customer your Deccan Bank account will be BLOCKED today. Update KYC immediately: http://deccanbank-kyc-update.co/verify
messages.explanation: Banks don't send KYC links from personal numbers. The web address imitates the bank. Open the official app or visit the branch instead.

messages.body: Practical exam schedule is on the school notice board and the school app. Please check your slot and bring your record book.
messages.explanation: A known contact sharing information without asking for money, data or links to unknown sites.

title: UPI tricks and fake jobs
intro: Scammers love UPI and online job offers. Review these five messages carefully. Look at what each one asks you to do.
objective: Understand that a PIN only sends money, and recognise fee-based job scams and impersonation calls.

messages.body: You have received a collect request: ₹2,000 CASHBACK REWARD. Enter your UPI PIN to receive the money in your account.
messages.explanation: A collect request takes money FROM you. Entering a PIN always sends money out; you never need a PIN to receive.

messages.body: Part-time job! Earn ₹3,000/day just liking videos from home. Limited seats. Pay ₹499 registration to start today.
messages.explanation: Real jobs pay you; they never charge registration. Easy money for liking videos is a classic task scam.

messages.body: Sir, suspicious transaction on your card. To stop it, tell me the OTP you just received. Quickly, otherwise money will be debited.
messages.explanation: Real bank staff never ask for an OTP. Hang up and call the number printed on your card or in the official app.

messages.body: Reminder: Post-matric scholarship applications close on 31 Oct. Apply only on the official scholarship portal. No fee is charged at any stage.
messages.explanation: It asks for nothing, says there is no fee and points you to the official portal. Open the portal yourself rather than through a forwarded link.

messages.body: Request: ₹120 for your share of yesterday's pizza 🍕
messages.explanation: A known friend requesting your share of a real expense. Paying it with your PIN is fine because you intend to send money.

title: Privacy, loan apps and social media
intro: Some scams target your personal data rather than your money directly. These five messages test whether you can protect your identity.
objective: Protect personal documents, avoid predatory loan apps and verify urgent requests from 'family'.

messages.body: You're selected for a FREE iPhone! Send a photo of your Aadhaar card and home address for delivery. Offer ends tonight!
messages.explanation: Aadhaar photos can be misused for fake loans and SIM cards. Real giveaways don't need your ID document.

messages.body: Instant ₹10,000 loan in 5 minutes, no documents! Just install and allow access to contacts, photos and SMS.
messages.explanation: Illegal loan apps harvest contacts and photos to harass borrowers. Regulated lenders check documents and never need your photo gallery.

messages.body: I will buy your old cycle for ₹3,000. Scan this QR code to RECEIVE the payment. Please do it now, I'm being transferred.
messages.explanation: Scanning a QR code and entering a PIN sends money. To receive, you only share your UPI ID; you never scan.

messages.sender: Unknown number: 'Hi it's your cousin Faiz, new number'
messages.body: Urgent!! I'm stuck, need ₹4,000 right now. Please don't tell Ammi, I'll return tomorrow. Send to this UPI.
messages.explanation: Call your cousin on the number you already have, or ask family. Requests for secrecy plus urgency are a classic impersonation pattern.

messages.body: Your electricity bill of ₹640 is due on 15th. Pay inside this app or at the payment counter.
messages.explanation: A notification inside an app you installed from the official store, asking you to pay inside the same app. No link, no data request.
